publications.title: Deterministic Data Flow Control Improves Agent Utility and Reduces Safety Violations
publications.subtitle: Very Large Data Bases ( VLDB ) - ICORE A*
publications.description: Today's agent safety mechanisms are largely ad hoc. By modeling agent-harness execution as relations, we can express declarative constraints over the agent's execution state and data flows, and return violation-specific feedback to steer the agent towards safety. Across four safety benchmarks, this reduces safety violations and improves task completion relative to nine SoTA defenses.

projects.title: Jane Street x Deterministic Schema Linking & Graph-Based Query Synthesis for Autonomous Agents
projects.description: Engineered a production-grade, deterministic text-to-SQL agentic pipeline designed to completely eliminate schema ambiguity, hallucinated columns, and missing structural joins under complex enterprise database schemas.Benchmark-Defeating Performance: Achieved a +8.1% improvement in Join Accuracy and a +2.2% boost in overall Execution Accuracy on the industry-standard BIRD benchmark, achieving 74.4% Join Accuracy.Graph-Algorithmic Optimization: Developed a minimal connecting subgraph extraction algorithm using foreign-key topologies to prune database schemas down to exact execution context prior to language model injection.Advanced Agentic Workflow: Designed a 5-stage pipeline featuring multi-phrase query expansion (Qwen-7B), hybrid dense-sparse retrieval unified via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), and massive-scale SQL generation (Qwen-32B).Fault-Tolerant Rewriter Layer: Created a deterministic query rewriter built with transactional Data Flow Control (DFC) and automated rollback guardrails, protecting the data store by reversing non-compliant or erroneous query logic on execution errors.

projects.title: SafeCoarsen: Privacy-Preserving Natural-Language Analytics via Deterministic Query Rewriting
projects.description: Researched and designed SafeCoarsen, an enterprise-grade data governance and access control engine built specifically to secure text-to-SQL and natural language data analytics interfaces. Zero-Trust AI Interception: Created a deterministic query rewriting engine that intercepts natural language analytical inputs, translating them into security-constrained expressions before compilation to prevent prompt injection and data exfiltration.Dynamic Access Control: Built structural abstractions to enforce strict role-based access control (RBAC) and privacy-preserving data-masking layers transparently within database processing paths. Enterprise Compliance Safeguards: Mitigated the non-deterministic privacy risks native to generative AI agents, ensuring all LLM-driven SQL generations are mathematically bound to corporate compliance policies.

projects.title: Provably Safe Data Flow Control & Algorithmic Policy Enforcement for LLM Agents
projects.description: Co-developed Data Flow Controls, an end-to-end, deep-tech data safety substrate that enforces regulatory, organizational, and user-defined policies over autonomous LLM agents.State-of-the-Art Architecture: Extended DuckDB by architecting custom asynchronous stream processing engine operators (AsyncSend/AsyncReceive) in C++ to logically split data flows and pipeline real-time compliance violations out of query execution paths. Multi-LLM Knowledge Graph Extraction: Engineered a cross-reference graph processing pipeline to ingest dense legal corpuses (e.g., 26 US Code). Implemented a majority-vote consensus framework leveraging Claude 4.6, GPT-5.4, and Gemini 3.1 Pro to assign execution-time confidence thresholds. Provenance-Aware Query Rewriting: Utilized provenance semirings to inject data flow control (DFC) predicates dynamically into runtime queries, guaranteeing mathematical compliance regarding data origins and lineages without execution overhead

This is an interesting picture to look at. These are the greenest programming languages in terms of energy usage. Interpreted languages like Python score very poor.. It's well clear it's purpose is fast to code, as a scripting and 'glue' language, it's a great dynamic typed language, but these features come at a great cost. I must say RUST is really starting to grow on me. It's almost equal to C and does much better than C++. They are doing an awesome job. I hope they can work a bit on cross-language compatibility to make it integrate with existing C++ code bases more easy. It will be interesting to see where Carbon stands in all this. source : https://lnkd.in/eaZJzHcP The original report with updated info: https://lnkd.in/ea-8jEyY The test was repeated in 2021 with even a more vastly set of tests. https://lnkd.in/eU2pET7J Python is mostly in the bottom half of rankings when it comes to energy consumption. It couldn’t even complete the Fibonacci task in 24 hours of the cut-off time. The researchers note that they “strictly followed” the CLBG project’s guidelines about compiler versions and the best optimization flags. Power consumption was measured using a tool from Intel — the Running Average Power Limit tool — with each program executed not just once, but 10 times, “to reduce the impact of cold starts and cache effects, and to be able to analyze the measurements’ consistency and avoid outliers.” the paper also includes a separate comparison of the different programming paradigms — including both functional and imperative programming, plus object-oriented programming and scripting. #golang #rust #c ++ #python #cloud #programming #language #language

One year at LTM . Seems like the fastest year of my career. When I look back, it's hard to believe how much has happened in twelve months. Building out and reimagining our delivery organisation. Pivoting decisively towards an AI-led delivery and talent model. Reimagining our core services while making sure we stayed deeply relevant to our clients. Sharpening our BlueVerse ecosystem. Rebranding the company as LTM. And setting the Outcreate theme that now runs through everything we do. Each of these on its own would have been a full year's work. Together, they made the last twelve months move at a pace I'm still catching my breath from. If this year taught me anything, it's that in today's world, everyone is a builder. Whether you're writing code, designing an experience, shaping a strategy, or simply solving a client's problem in a smarter way — building isn't a job title anymore, it's a mindset. And there's a particular kind of joy that comes from building together, not alone. Watching ideas turn into outcomes because a whole team leaned in. That's the thing I keep coming back to when I think about this year. Not a milestone or a metric, but the memories I built along the way with our phenomenal teams — our Outcreators — across India and around the globe. The late-night calls that turned into laughs. The problems we solved together. The trust we built, one delivery at a time. That's been the real joy of this year. Thank you to every Outcreator who has been with me on this journey. And if this is what one year looks like, I can't wait to see what's next. There's so much more to come. Here's to Year Two, and to building together. 🚀 #WorkAnniversary #LTM #Outcreate #Outcreators

Back from Winterthur and still processing that the ZHAW entrepreneurship HealthTech Summer School is actually over! 2.5 weeks ago we got handed a clinical need and told: go build a real seed-stage pitch out of it. Needs analysis, concept testing, IP, regulatory, reimbursement, all through Stanford University 's Biodesign Process. Under three weeks. No pressure. My team built "Glyra" - an AI-powered menstrual cycle intelligence for women with Type 1 diabetes. I spent most of my time on the technical side, figuring out how to build a cycle-aware AI engine that actually learns how a woman's body responds to hormones, CGM data, insulin, sleep, all of it, and turns that into insulin guidance that's actually personalized instead of one-size-fits-all. Going from "wait, this gap in diabetes tech is real and nobody's solved it" to an actual pitch-ready platform in this timeframe was a lot, honestly. But so worth it. Florian Zimmermann , Mariia Gurova , Vanessa Vogt ~ you three made this the best kind of chaotic. Genuinely couldn't have asked for a better team to build with. And thank you ZHAW School of Management and Law for putting together a program this good. A huge shout-out to the organizers as well - Jens Haarmann, PhD, Mathias B. , Nicole Z, Mario Kratter ! Also just - the people! The late nights, the pre-pitch panic, the random conversations that turned into real friendships. That part I didn't expect and it might be the part I'm most grateful for. Onto whatever's next! 🚀

This summer, one of my goals was to become more industry-ready by building skills beyond the classroom and developing a deeper understanding of modern AI frameworks and their real-world possibilities. As part of that journey, I built ContextCue - an agentic AI system that transforms recorded meetings into searchable, persistent, and actionable organizational memory. Your team’s memory, on cue. Most meeting tools treat each meeting as an isolated transcript or summary. I wanted to explore a broader idea: meetings should contribute to a continuously accessible layer of organizational knowledge. Important decisions often become separated from the reasoning behind them. Action items lose context, unresolved questions are forgotten, and teams struggle to reconstruct why a direction was chosen weeks or months later. Consider a business executive preparing for a client follow-up. They may remember that a pricing proposal was rejected, but not the client’s exact concern, the alternatives discussed, or who agreed to revise it. Instead of searching through recordings, notes, emails, and chats, they could ask: “Why was the original pricing proposal rejected, what alternative was discussed, and what did we agree to do next?” ContextCue retrieves relevant information across meetings, generates a grounded response with timestamp citations, identifies related action items and open questions, and can prepare a contextual follow-up. The same idea could help engineering teams track technical decisions, consulting and sales teams retain client context, research groups follow evolving findings, and project handoffs preserve reasoning that might otherwise be lost. The system can: • Search semantically across meetings • Retrieve decisions and supporting discussions • Generate grounded answers with timestamp citations • Identify action items, owners, and open questions • Prepare follow-ups using previous context • Preserve continuity across recurring conversations What interested me most was not simply building another transcription or meeting-summary tool, but exploring how AI could preserve the reasoning, commitments, and context behind organizational decisions. The system uses an agent layer with intent routing and tool-based retrieval. I also built an evaluation workflow to verify that relevant context is retrieved before generating a response, since reliable retrieval is essential for trustworthy AI. Built with Python, FastAPI, Faster-Whisper, Qdrant, Ollama, Streamlit, FFmpeg, RAG, SQLite, MCP, and vector search. There is still so much more I want to build, improve, and learn through this project. I’m excited to keep experimenting and expanding ContextCue. A special thank you to my mentor, Rajeshwari Ganesan , for her guidance, feedback, and support. It was inspiring to learn from someone so accomplished with deep AI experience. #AgenticAI #GenerativeAI #AIAgents #RAG #AIEngineering #FastAPI #Python #SoftwareEngineering #MCP

This day, 28 years ago, my father passed away after a case of undiagnosed pneumonia. 1998 was the year I graduated from business school. I had a couple of months at home before joining my first job. Dad developed a low grade fever and struggled every day - I went with him to several doctors and even got specialists to see his chest x-ray. They couldn't diagnose the pneumonia that was developing. It was devastating. I turned this grief into a passion for healthcare. Since then, I have felt an acute need for better tools to make sure that every disease is diagnosed at the earliest possible moment, so we have the most amount of time to cure it. Today Qure.ai (that we spun off from Fractal in 2020) has touched more than 50 million lives to diagnose patients with TB and lung cancer. A couple of weeks ago, we signed with Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation to extend Vaidya.ai support to Mumbai's government hospitals and doctors in improving the quality of care. And last month, I also joined the board of Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Laboratories, arguably India's most respected pharmaceutical company as an independent director. These are small steps in contributing to a big cause. Advances in AI should fundamentally reshape health outcomes for the entire planet - better diagnosis, better quality of care for every patient, and novel drugs that improve health outcomes and improve healthspan of the entire population. Prashant Warier Suraj Amonkar Prasad G V Ashwini Bhide
